quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Cleveland Cavaliers' roster depth and salary cap constraints
quotes.excerpt: Sam Merrill was their 10th or 11th man. They had a very deep team.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Two years ago when they were a 60-win team, they had a $165 million payroll. Part of that was because Evan Mobley was still on his rookie contract. That was the year he won Defensive Player of the Year. At that time, it was arguable that Sam Merrill was their 10th or 11th man, depending on where you wanted to rank certain guys on the roster. They had a very deep team. DeAndre Hunter, they had Ty Jerome, they had Isaac Okoro, they had Dean Wade, etc. What I am arriving at, Bobby, especially looking at this now, is that they arguably now, Sam Merrill is their sixth man because they have hollowed out their depth and had to spend on signing a lot of their players.

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: Well, the payroll has gone from $165 million to almost $210 million. They also have no tradeable first-round picks and one tradeable second-round pick, and they are $45,000 below the hard cap of the first apron, which they are first-apron hard-capped because they signed and traded for Max Strus.

quotes.social_post: Brian Windhorst notes the Cavaliers have hollowed out their depth to pay their core, leaving them with limited trade assets and sitting right against the first apron hard cap.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Cleveland's poor performance with their core lineup
quotes.excerpt: They have the third-worst five-man lineup out there at a minus-19 per 100.
quotes.quote: If you are a Cleveland fan listening, put your hands over your ears about this number I am about to give you. They have the third-worst five-man lineup out there at a minus-19 per 100 when the group of James Harden, Evan Mobley, and Jarrett Allen is on the court.
quotes.social_post: Bobby Marks highlights a concerning stat for Cleveland fans, noting their core lineup of James Harden, Evan Mobley, and Jarrett Allen has been the third worst five-man unit in the league.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Why the Cavaliers cannot trade Jarrett Allen
quotes.excerpt: You can't trade Jarrett Allen unless you are getting a center back.
quotes.quote: You can't trade Jarrett Allen unless you are getting a center back. The reason you can't is because Evan Mobley has not proven he can be their starting center. He has not proven it.
quotes.social_post: Brian Windhorst argues the Cavaliers cannot trade Jarrett Allen unless they get a center back, stating Evan Mobley has not yet proven he can handle the starting center role.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Bontemps' evaluation of Evan Mobley's best position
quotes.excerpt: I still think Evan Mobley's best position is center.
quotes.quote: I still think Evan Mobley's best position is center.
quotes.social_post: Tim Bontemps maintains his stance that Evan Mobley's best position in the NBA is playing center.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Why Evan Mobley is not a full-time center
quotes.excerpt: He doesn't compete at the level that he needs to compete to be a full-time center.
quotes.quote: You are in a massive amount of people in the NBA who believe that, but I am telling you, if you put him there as your full-time center, the Cavaliers have tried this. He doesn't compete at the level that he needs to compete to be a full-time center. He obviously does it in the fourth quarter of games because their best lineups are with him at center. But if you put him at center full-time, I am telling you, the data set is not favorable.
quotes.social_post: Brian Windhorst pushes back on the idea of Evan Mobley as a full-time center, claiming the data is not favorable and he does not compete at the necessary level for the full game.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden's decline in playmaking and free throw rate
quotes.excerpt: More concerning is his playmaking is down. He's only averaging five assists.
quotes.quote: James Harden is shooting 36 percent, the lowest of his career. More concerning is his playmaking is down. He's only averaging five assists, despite getting the same minutes. That's the fewest number of assists he's averaged since he got traded to Houston. His free throws, which are obviously a very key metric, he's only averaging four free throws a game. James Harden is not built to get two trips to the foul line a game.
quotes.social_post: Brian Windhorst breaks down James Harden's struggles, noting his shooting percentage, assist numbers, and free throw rate are all trending in the wrong direction.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Pressure on Kenny Atkinson due to roster limitations
quotes.excerpt: In Cleveland now, the pressure is being applied to Kenny Atkinson.
quotes.quote: In Cleveland now, the pressure is being applied to Kenny Atkinson. I understand why that pressure is being applied to him because they are not functionally able to really make a roster change. When that pressure is happening, it just naturally goes to the coach.
quotes.social_post: Brian Windhorst explains that pressure is mounting on Kenny Atkinson in Cleveland because the roster is functionally locked in and cannot be easily changed.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden's struggles and lack of burst
quotes.excerpt: He doesn't have burst, he doesn't have lift.
quotes.quote: Is this a slow start for James Harden or a steep decline? He doesn't have burst, he doesn't have lift. He does have a three-year guaranteed contract that by the way was part of the maneuvering.
quotes.social_post: Bobby Marks questions if James Harden is just off to a slow start or in a steep decline, pointing to a clear lack of burst and lift on the floor.
